feature: Customer Portal v2 -- MICROSOFT CHANGES (/portal-v2/ms-changes), recreated from 'Microsoft Changes.dc.html'. Microsoft ships in waves; pick a wave and the page becomes that wave. A density grid over eleven uneven time buckets grouped into five waves, the tenant's own freeze windows drawn over it, and for the selected wave: a header card with four tiles and 'Brief this wave', 'What stops working', 'Decide before it lands' (with snooze / record-a-decision overlays), 'Nothing to do', 'What your people will see' (the seen-in-the-wild list), the per-group impact panel, an ownership line, and a 'Did this release?' retrospective for the two landed waves. Each post opens in an eleven-section detail slide-over -- Microsoft's own words beside the tenant's counted answer, evidence, consequence, phases, who-was-told, history, and a thread with the architect. PART 10 built every surface listed as deferred by the earlier pass.
notes: THE LOGIN BLOCK IS NOT OPTIONAL. /portal-v2/* sits behind ProtectedRoute.
UI ROUTE SHAPE: /portal/{slug}/portal-v2/ms-changes/{wave}. App.tsx declares '/portal-v2/ms-changes/:wave' BEFORE '/portal-v2/ms-changes', and both before '/portal-v2/:pillar'.
shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree.

THE WAVE SLUGS ARE NOT THE PROTOTYPE'S KEYS -- late-august / september / q2 / q3 / beyond -- because this is a URL a customer is meant to be able to send. MSC10-14 pin the mapping and the summed counts (35 / 80 / 100), read off the DOM so the sum is proven rather than typed.

ROUND TWO, ITEM 6: the density ROWS are the fluid repeat(11,1fr) shape with no min-width floor. The WAVE BAND above them KEEPS its overflow-x:auto + min-width:820px (Microsoft Changes.dc.html 165-166) because eleven month columns plus a 190px label need the width. Reproducing the band's scroll is faithful, not an oversight.

THE POST DETAIL IS A SLIDE-OVER WITH AN ELEVEN-SECTION RAIL, one section shown at a time. MSC30-34 click the rail (pv2-msc-sec-*) and assert the section that comes up, which is why the many strings are spread across steps rather than asserted in one expanded row.

THE RETROSPECTIVE IS REACHED VIA THE 'Landed' STRIP (pv2-msc-pastnav-*), which the design renders as pastNav; the active markup carries no live-wave column for a past wave, so a small strip is the reachable entry point. Selecting a landed wave replaces the live sections with 'Did this release?'; navigating to any live wave (a URL change) drops back out of it.
THERE IS NO NEGATIVE TEXT ASSERTION IN THIS HARNESS, and an array in textContains is ANY-of, not all-of. Every all-of assertion here is its own step.
NO `select` STEPS in the asserted flow. The forms' selects live in the right FormDrawer and are not driven here.
ENV VARS required: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD.
